name: NICE Clinical Knowledge Summaries (CKS)
owner: Clarity Informatics Ltd (04133376), trading as Agilio Software | Primary Care; ultimately funds advised by Five Arrows (Rothschild & Co) and TA Associates. Commissioned and paid for by NICE.
type: point-of-care primary care guidance (publicly commissioned, privately owned)
whoCanRead: NHS clinicians and individuals in the UK, Crown Dependencies and British Overseas Territories, for personal or educational use; non-UK IPs blocked; organisations and universities need a commercial licence
cost: Free at point of use in UK (NICE pays: £882,000 for 2017-20; £1,320,000 (FTS) / £1,323,000 (Contracts Finder) for 8 Apr 2023 - 7 Apr 2026, 1 tender received)
licence: Excluded from NICE UK Open Content Licence; 'The content within CKS is the intellectual property of Agilio'; scraping and data mining prohibited
openAlternative: NICE guidelines (free to read, UK-only reuse licence); NHG-Standaarden (NL) for some topics
citation: NICE CKS block page (403) and https://www.nice.org.uk/cks-is-only-available-in-the-uk ; https://agiliosoftware.com/primary-care/clinical-knowledge-summaries/ ; Contracts Finder f1a9e595-1503-429f-8ccc-10711d78dbf0 and 883b3776-c848-4589-96fe-9ff6eeb58871 ; Find a Tender 2023/S 000-011488 ; NICE CKS guide PDF (2015)
whatWasRead: block page; licence pages; contract notices (web pages); NICE CKS guide (full text); Agilio licensing page
notes: Origin: PRODIGY, Sowerby Centre for Health Informatics, Newcastle (1995-98 research; national rollout 1999-2000; PMID 10566381). NICE-funded Clarity contract since Sept 2012. Prof Ian Purves (PRODIGY lead) was Clarity director 2000-2021. Status of contract after 7 Apr 2026 unknown. Topics updated at least every 5 years; 'more than 65 topics' a year; NICE-accredited process (2015 statement).

name: Agilio Prodigy / Agilio: Diagnosis and Treatment Guidance (CKS content sold outside UK)
owner: Agilio Software (Clarity Informatics); resold by Pharmaceutical Press (Royal Pharmaceutical Society) via MedicinesComplete
whoCanRead: Paying subscribers; Prodigy site requires account (only 'Asthma' marked free)
openAlternative: none equivalent; national society guidelines where they exist
citation: Pharmaceutical Press product page; prodigy.clarity.co.uk home page; NICE 'CKS is only available in the UK' page
whatWasRead: product page and site home page (topic list); no topic content opened
notes: Pharmaceutical Press page: 'Covering over 370 clinical topics ... Available to customers outside of the UK', 'Clinical topics commissioned and accredited by NICE', '~7 New topics produced each year'. Prodigy lists Insomnia, Obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome, Restless legs syndrome, Sleep disorders - shift work and jet lag. Clarity's FY2025 accounts say turnover 'arises wholly within the United Kingdom' (£8,908k), so overseas revenue location unclear.

name: British National Formulary (BNF) and BNF for Children (BNFc)
owner: Royal Pharmaceutical Society of Great Britain (Pharmaceutical Press), BMJ Publishing Group Ltd, RCPCH Publications Ltd
whoCanRead: Via NICE: NHS and UK public for personal reference (block page says England, Scotland and Wales; bnf-uk-only page includes Northern Ireland); Crown Dependencies and Overseas Territories excluded; overseas via MedicinesComplete subscription
cost: Free at point of use in UK; NICE contract £15,160,000, 1 Apr 2021 - 31 Mar 2033, direct award
licence: Copyright of the three owners; excluded from NICE open licence; non-NHS bodies must license (licensing@rpharms.com); scraping and data mining banned
openAlternative: emc / medicines.org.uk (UK SmPCs and leaflets, no registration); MHRA Products; EMA product information; DailyMed (US); WHO eEML (list only)
citation: Contracts Finder b2504f68-a7fd-46ce-87ae-e3e3a42f3fdc ; Find a Tender 2022/S 000-005873 ('Direct award due to IPR ownership') ; BNF block page ; https://www.nice.org.uk/bnf-uk-only ; https://www.pharmaceuticalpress.com/who-we-serve/nhs/
whatWasRead: block page; NICE info page; contract notices (web pages); publisher NHS page
notes: Negotiated procedure without prior publication because the owners hold the copyright. InPublishing (2021-08-24) quotes 'over 6 million times a year' use on MedicinesComplete (publisher claim).

name: NICE guidelines (contrast case)
owner: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (public body)
licence: NICE UK Open Content Licence: 'UK-only, royalty-free'; international reuse needs a permission form; AI use not covered and needs permission
openAlternative: (is itself the open alternative for reading)
citation: NICE UK open content licence page and form page
notes: Open to read, not open to reuse outside the UK or for AI. Excludes CKS, BNF, NCC 'full' guideline versions and economic models.

name: UpToDate
whoCanRead: Subscribers; national free access for health personnel in Norway (Helsebiblioteket, new 3-year deal from 1 April 2026); reported national access in Mongolia (from Dec 2020) and Saudi Arabia (from 2014)
cost: Individual price not confirmed; search summary of Wolters Kluwer Philippines page: '$579 / year Starting price' (verify)
whatWasRead: Helsebiblioteket notice (web page); Serials abstract; Mongolia/Saudi only via search summaries (vendor releases 403)
notes: Norway first bought national UpToDate and BMJ Best Practice licences after a 2009 tender (Serials 2011).

name: BMJ Best Practice
whoCanRead: Subscribers; all NHS staff and learners in England (NICE-procured National Core Content, framework announced Nov 2023); everyone in Republic of Ireland via Health Library Ireland (announced March 2023); Norway access ENDED 1 April 2026
whatWasRead: subscribe page; BMJ press releases; Helsebiblioteket notice (web pages)
notes: When Norway's licence ended, Helsebiblioteket deleted all translated BMJ patient leaflets because it no longer had the rights to publish them.

name: DynaMed
whoCanRead: Subscribers (institutional and individual); regional consortium licences (e.g. eHLbc, British Columbia)
cost: Not found (prices rendered by JavaScript on vendor site)
citation: EBSCO DynaMed page; JMLA 2021 doi:10.5195/jmla.2021.1176 (UpToDate vs DynaMed accuracy)
whatWasRead: vendor page (no price visible); eHLbc via search summary only

name: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG / TG)
whoCanRead: Subscribers; some state health staff via library proxies
cost: 12-month subscriptions; mirrored page lists $378 (AUD assumed; verify)
openAlternative: Australian Prescriber (free journal, same publisher); NPS/ACSQHC materials
whatWasRead: about and subscribe pages (price not rendered statically)
notes: 'no reliance on any form of government funding or commercial interests ... relying on the Australian healthcare community to fund the guidelines through subscriptions'. Roots in antibiotic guidelines from January 1978.

name: Australian Medicines Handbook (AMH)
owner: Australian Medicines Handbook Pty Ltd (not checked)
openAlternative: TGA product information; emc-style regulator labels
notes: Australia's BNF-equivalent is also closed. Ownership and price not verified.

name: HealthPathways
owner: Streamliners (New Zealand); localised and run by regional health bodies (e.g. PHNs in Australia, districts in NZ)
country: New Zealand, Australia, UK and others (regional sites)
type: regional clinical pathways (who to refer, where, when)
whoCanRead: Clinicians and practice staff in the region, with a personal login; not the public
cost: Free to eligible clinicians ('There is no cost to access', Western Victoria PHN)
licence: Proprietary platform; regional content behind login
openAlternative: none; national guidelines cover what to do but not local referral routes
whatWasRead: PHN access page; HealthPathways vendor home page
notes: 'not designed to be used by the general public and can only be accessed by using a secure login and password'. Shared logins being retired for personal accounts (search summaries). Melbourne PHN OSA/insomnia pathways could not be read (canada-oceania-latam note).

name: Map of Medicine
owner: Originally UCL and Royal Free Hampstead NHS Trust (2001); later Hearst / Informa (order unclear)
openAlternative: HealthPathways (replaced it in e.g. Brisbane North, from 2017)
notes: Referrals and sidebar tools withdrawn from sale on 31 March 2018; pathways map ceased 30 June 2018. Was integrated into EMIS and TPP. Shows that commercial pathway content can disappear.

name: AWMF Leitlinienregister (incl. DEGAM and DGSM guidelines)
owner: AWMF (association of German scientific medical societies) and member societies
whoCanRead: Anyone (free to read), but the site has a bot wall
cost: Free on the register; journal versions (e.g. Springer Somnologie) can be paywalled
licence: Register reserves its texts against text-and-data mining (§44b UrhG) and AI use (per europe.md)
whatWasRead: AWMF rules page; register blocked by Anubis bot wall here
notes: Open to read, closed to machines.

citation: europe.json rows read richtlijnen.nhg.org/standaarden/slaapproblemen as a web page
